hook: SCP-3984 is an end-of-the-world file where the apocalypse is that no animal, humans included, can die anymore. It is wrapped in a second-person story: you have broken into a closed library at night to read this document on a hacked terminal, looking for the answer to a mystery you've carried for twenty-four years. The experiment logs inside are graphic, covering strangulation, exsanguination, decapitation and a brain put through a blender.
whyItMatters:
It belongs to the End of Death series and its ΩK scenario, and it shows how much an end-of-world premise changes once you think it through. Immortality here brings no healing and no youth, only the inability to stop, and the file spells out the overpopulation and starvation that follow.

The framing turns a standard report into a scene. Your interruptions after each log tell you something about yourself before the file ever says it outright.
thingsToNotice:
Dr. Young's opening memo bans any research into reversing ΩK or finding its cause, and the narrator immediately flags that as odd. Her experiments then escalate with no stated purpose, until she shoots herself in the head on New Year's Eve 2025 and is left unable to move or communicate; Dr. Michaels takes over and moves to monkeys, finding that what really can't be switched off is consciousness, even in brain cells suspended in saline.

The twist sits in Experiment 10. When D-11424 is guillotined and the injury is called irreparable, the narrator smiles and touches a ring-shaped scar around their own neck, so the reader has been the decapitated D-Class all along. The deeper answer is locked behind Level 5 access; the Foundation arrives, a bullet passes through the desk and through your chest, and the story ends with you wishing you could die.
